algorithm: PPO (brax PPO, primary; also SAC and a torch-based RSL-RL PPO comparison for locomotion)
arm: Franka Emika Panda (+ Robotiq gripper for the non-prehensile block task); Aloha bi-arm platform (peg insertion, non-dexterous)
sim: MJX (MuJoCo XLA, JAX-based GPU branch of MuJoCo) with the Madrona batch renderer for on-device vision
success_criterion: within 3 cm of the goal position and within 10 degrees of the desired orientation (non-prehensile block-reorientation task, Sec. IV-C2-a)
headline_metric: consecutive successful rotations before failure (LEAP Hand real-world cube reorientation)
headline_value: median 3.5, mean 7.1 consecutive successful rotations across 10 real-world trials (Table I)
paper_code_mismatch: The shipped code adds a second, tendon-driven hand (TetherIA Aero Hand Open, aero_hand/) with its own RotateZAxis task, nowhere mentioned in the paper text, which discusses only the LEAP Hand; do not attribute Aero Hand results or DoF to this paper.
note_gaps:
MJX's contact cost scales with possible geom pairs, not active contacts (JAX static-shape requirement), requiring per-environment max_contact_points/max_geom_pairs tuning (Table III) not reflected in a single reward_terms count; the code-derived cube-spin reward (angvel + 5 cost terms) is a different task/reward design from the paper's headline CubeReorient task, whose own reward-term count is not enumerated in the paper text, so reward_terms is left null. LEAP-hand Table I per-trial rotation counts have an OCR ambiguity around trials 7-8 ('4
1'). Real-hardware trial counts differ by deployment: LEAP hand 10 (used above as the headline), non-prehensile Franka+Robotiq block reorientation 35 trials (85.7% mean success), pixel-based Franka pick-cube 12 trials (100% success). The cross-simulator throughput comparison vs. IsaacLab/ManiSkill3 is explicitly flagged by the authors as non-rigorous.
